messages:
maria-ml: Quick QA run on the new open-vector-1024-q4 model. Ran recall@1/5/10 on the semantic-sim test set (~50k queries). Posting aggregated numbers and a quick failure-mode summary, want 👀 before we promote to a canary rollout.

maria-ml: Summary (baseline = fp16 1024, candidate = q4 1024):
- recall@1: baseline 0.780, candidate 0.752
- recall@5: baseline 0.920, candidate 0.902
- recall@10: baseline 0.960, candidate 0.951
- avg embed latency: baseline 18.4ms, candidate 12.0ms (~35% speedup)
- 99p latency: baseline 65ms, candidate 48ms

maria-ml: clustering metrics: silhouette baseline 0.43 -> candidate 0.40, cluster purity (top-1) 0.86 -> 0.84.

maria-ml: quick command used to reproduce:
```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model open-vector-1024 --quant q4 --dataset semsim_50k \
  --batch 1024 --metric recall@1,5,10 --save-output /tmp/q4-eval.json
```

embed-bot: Eval job 1768009901 finished. Artifacts: /artifacts/1768009901/q4-eval.json (s3).

samir: thanks — degradation is small but measurable. Do we have per-length / per-domain breakdowns?

maria-ml: Yes — short queries (<6 tokens) see largest drop (recall@1 down ~4.5 pts). Medium (6-20) down ~2.5 pts. Long queries (>20) negligible diff. Domain-wise: product-name disambiguation and punctuation-heavy queries show issues.

toni: any weird nearest-neighbor collisions? examples?

maria-ml: A couple of examples attached in artifacts: candidate maps "apple inc" -> consumer_brand instead of company when punctuation variants in the query. Also some near-duplicates merged differently after quantization — likely due to lower precision in tail dims.

evan: Can we re-run with per-dim pruning off and high-recall quant config? I want to see tradeoffs before canary.

maria-ml: I ran one alt config (q4+fp-backend on topk dims): recall@1 0.762, recall@5 0.908, latency ~13.5ms. Better than q4 default but still not baseline. Saved as /artifacts/1768010003/q4-mix.json.

samir: Proposal: canary 5% of traffic on Dedicated pool with fallback to fp16 model on misses; monitor recall@5 and per-route error. Rollback if recall@5 drop >1.5 pts or latency improvement <20% (we want a meaningful perf win). Thoughts?

toni: +1 to metric-based rollback. Also add clustering drift alert (silhouette drop >0.03) and a small eval set of critical queries (top 1k business queries).

maria-ml: I can wire a canary config in staging (deploy flag + routing policy) and schedule a 24h A/B. Will also run targeted eval on top1k and short-query subset pre/post. Plan: start canary tomorrow 10:00 PDT.

evan: Sounds good. Add a smoke test that fails the rollout if any route has recall@5 drop >2 pts.

maria-ml: Will do. I'll post the canary config and a short runbook when it's ready. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
